moon_base/all.explanation: [PSI-99] SAFFIRE-II (84.8/100) and [PSI-98] SAFFIRE-I (84.3/100) rank highest because both match the scenario's ventilated airflow (15/15), test solid habitat materials (20/20), cover the prevention pillar (14/20), and achieve full richness scores (10/10). In contrast, [PSI-68] FLEX-2 (77.0/100) ranks third because it tests liquid droplet fuels with no named habitat materials (4/20), even though its tested oxygen range fully matches the 30% scenario (35/35) alongside matching the ventilated airflow (15/15).

iss_cabin/all.explanation: [PSI-98] SAFFIRE-I and [PSI-99] SAFFIRE-II rank highest with identical total scores of 93.4/100 because both feature 20 cm/s airflow matching the ventilated scenario, oxygen levels just 0.5 points away from the 21% target, and full points for habitat materials and data richness. [PSI-25] BASS-II ranks third with a total score of 82.0/100, achieving full points for tested oxygen encompassing the 21% target, covering two pillars (prevention, suppression), and scoring maximum points for habitat materials and richness. However, [PSI-25] BASS-II received 0/15 points for airflow because it was not reported, placing it below the top two.

spacesuit/all.explanation: SAFFIRE-I [PSI-98] (49.0/100), SAFFIRE-II [PSI-99] (49.0/100), and SAFFIRE-III [PSI-100] (49/100) rank highest because all three earned full points (20/20) for testing solid fuels including habitat materials. In addition, each investigation received maximum richness scores (10/10) for including experimental tables and 5 measurement types, as well as 14/20 points for covering the prevention pillar. Even with reduced scores for ventilated airflow (5/15) and oxygen testing (0/35), these combined category results place them at the top.

moon_base/detection.explanation:
All three investigations—[PSI-102], [PSI-101], and [PSI-60]—rank highest because they each earn full points (20/20) for covering the detection focus. 

First-ranked [PSI-102] achieves a total score of 64/100 by earning points for matching ventilated airflow (15/15), testing solid habitat materials like silicone and Kapton (20/20), and having high data richness (9/10). 

Second-ranked [PSI-101] follows with a 50/100 total score by matching solid habitat materials like foam and Kapton (20/20) and earning a 10/10 richness score despite missing airflow data, whereas third-ranked [PSI-60] scores 28/100 due to lower richness (2/10), unreported airflow, and using gaseous fuels rather than habitat materials.
